almanac: 548: the plate does not fill edge to edge. There are blank white strips down the left and right of the top frame (about x 0-12 and above y 18 in the corners), and the bottom scroll band below the pedestal is inset about 40 px each side, leaving white wedges at both bottom corners. Both break the no-white-over-12px rule. Run the ground and ornament to all four edges at every height.

548: the thin ruled rectangle around the upper field is a hard box, and so is the beaded/knurled rule across the top at 240 and 90. The top edge has to rise out of the content as scroll tips or a broken moulding, not a closed outline.

Scrollwork reads as scattered, separately stamped leaf clusters floating on a flat ground, not the Codex's big continuous volutes. At 548 the eight-plus small curled-leaf fragments in the corners and the bottom band are near-identical stamps. Replace them with two or three large S-volutes per side that spring from the pedestal, spiral into tight shaded eyes, overlap, and wrap the cartouche, the way the Codex scrolls do.

The ground is one uniform horizontal hatch across the whole plate, which reads as wallpaper. Cut it away behind the relief with a darker cross-hatch or stipple so the leaves pop, and give leaves dark undercut shadows on the ground side.

Leaf modelling is still mostly outline plus a patch of hatch. Shading must follow the form (dark into each curl, light on the turned edge), with central and secondary veins and serrated lobes on every leaf.

The cartouche subject is too thin and diagrammatic. The armillary sphere is plain outline rings with no bulino shading on its bands or stand. The St. Johns Bridge towers look like smooth obelisks/Golden Gate pylons: they need the pointed gothic arch openings and the steel-lattice texture. The Loy Krathong float and the heron are too small to read at e-ink size. Enlarge and fully engrave these figures with metal, feather and wood texture.

The pedestal tablet's lunar phase row is 18 identical small circles in a strip, which is exactly the medallion row the brief bans. Draw fewer, larger phases with real shaded crescents, set in carved frames or inside a scroll, and make today's ring clearly read.

90: four mirrored copies of the same leaf cluster either side of an oval sticker medallion is a repetitive stamped frieze. Make one continuous running scroll that flows into the medallion and terminates, and integrate the medallion into the scroll rather than floating it on the ground.
The hourglass at 548 is small and sits in a gap. Grow it out of the crest scrolls as a figural element at Codex scale.
No s*-onpage render exists, so flow from the content above cannot be verified. Produce an on-page proof (for example with a forced test room) before resubmitting.
index: Scrollwork is not Codex-grade: leaves are spiky, jagged and scattered like crumpled paper, not big confident C/S scrolls spiralling into tight curls. Rebuild the volutes as a few large, continuous acanthus scrolls per side, each with a clean spine curve, overlapping leaf lobes (rounded and serrated, not saw-toothed shards), a central vein plus secondary veins, and a tight spiral eye at every terminal.

Shading is flat crosshatch patches dropped on leaves. Make bulino/parallel hatching follow each leaf's form: dense and dark into the curl and under each overlap, fading to a clean white highlight on the turned edge, so every leaf reads as rounded relief.

The ground is a flat field of horizontal ruled lines at uniform density, which reads as cheap wallpaper and as a hard rectangle. Cut it away properly: dark stipple or fine contour-following line shading that darkens next to the relief (cast shadow) and lightens toward open areas, and vignette or feather it at the top and sides so the plate flows out of the content above instead of sitting in a ruled box with a hard top edge.

The heron-neck scroll stems are unreadable: they look like pens or clamps poking into the cartouche. Carve a recognisable heron head (crest plume, eye, long dagger bill, feathered neck in bulino) growing out of the leaf scroll, the way the Codex faces grow from the leafwork. If it can't read as a heron at 570 px, drop it.

The vignette is crude. The St. Johns Bridge towers look like fountain pens or striped posts, not gothic towers (they need pointed arches, spires and tapered piers). Mt. Hood is a bare outline triangle; it needs glaciers, ridges and shaded flanks. The clouds are flat stacked bubbles, and the sun with its starburst is clip-art. The heron is a thin outline with no feather texture. Re-engrave the scene with tonal line work: sky hatching graded toward the sun, cumulus modelled with curved hatching, layered dark treeline and cattail reeds, and water with reflections.

The cartouche frame is a plain thick rounded rectangle made of concentric strokes. Make it a carved moulding: bead and reel or a gadrooned edge, inner shadowed bevel, and acanthus leaves overlapping the frame so the scrolls interlock with it rather than floating beside it.
The ribbon banner is a flat white strip with thin outline lettering. Give it folds, shaded undersides, forked tails tucked behind the scrolls, and heavier engraved lettering.

The tall-sheet pedestal is a flat stack of ruled bars with a row of identical beads and two tiny circle rosettes, and below it is a separate strip of small scattered scroll stamps. Make it architectural: a knurled bar shaded to look cylindrical, a moulded tablet with depth, and one continuous bottom scroll composition (as in the Codex base) instead of stamped bits. The Blazers pinwheel rosette is too small and generic to read as an Easter egg; enlarge it and carve it.

In the 570x90 frieze the scrolls repeat as near-identical units marching in a row (stamping), and the medallion is a plain oval sticker. Use a continuous running scroll that changes direction and size, and set the medallion inside it with a leaf collar.

E-ink: in the -eink renders the ruled ground goes uniform mid-grey and the leaf hatching muddies into it, so the relief doesn't separate from the ground. Increase contrast: darker ground right behind the scrolls, and more white highlight on the leaf edges.

On-page (s1 and s3), the plate reads as a separate dark box pasted between the content and the buttons, with a band of the page's diagonal hatch still visible beneath it. Confirm it fills the whole free rectangle and blends into the page frame at its edges.
almanac-01: The plate does not appear on the page. In s1-550x404-onpage.png the whole 404px area under 'New Year's Day' is plain diagonal wallpaper hatch: no krathong, scrolls or pedestal. This is the 'cheap wallpaper' Parker already rejected. Find out why the plate is not composited (wrong size or slot, or the page ground painted over it) and re-check the on-page render before claiming done.

The leafwork is not acanthus at Codex level. The leaves are claw- or tongue-shaped crescents with sawtooth edges and flat hatch blocks, with no central vein, no secondary veins, no lobed leaflets that turn over, and no tight spiral eyes (the 'eyes' are a plain dot inside a C hook). Rebuild them as modelled acanthus: shading in bulino lines that follow the curve, dark into the curl, a white turned edge, and real spiral volutes.

The 90px (and 60px) frieze is stamped. The same scroll unit repeats four times, mirrored, around a small oval. That breaks the 'no repetitive stamping' rule. Make it one continuous rinceau that grows out of the medallion and runs to both ends, with leaves that vary in size and turn.

The 548px bottom band under the pedestal is a row of four sparse, disconnected scroll fragments on a horizontal-line ground. It reads as filler. Either flow continuous scrolls into it or end the composition with a proper base (knurled bar, beading, and pendant acanthus like the Codex's lower volutes).

The vignette is drawn too thinly. The moon is a hatched disc, the chedis are small blobs, and the heron is a pale outline with almost no feather texture. The krathong is the subject and is only about 60px wide at 548px. Enlarge it and give it more relief: shaded banana-leaf folds, petals on the marigold dome, and wood-grain bulino on the base disc.

The Veterans Day star ribbon is a flat straight band with stamped stars, and the Thanksgiving tablet's wheat garland is a faint line of chevrons. The ribbon needs real folds, turned ends and shading, and the garland needs engraved wheat ears and a pumpkin with volume.

The scrolls sit on a flat horizontal-line ground inside a hard rectangular rule, so the plate reads as a framed box. The top edge should rise from the content above, with scroll tips breaking past the edge and no full-width rule (see the 240 and 548 tops).
almanac-02: Leafwork is not acanthus. Every 'leaf' is the same banana or crab-claw shape with a jagged edge, scattered across the ground as separate pieces. The Codex has continuous stems that spiral into tight curls, with leaves that overlap and wrap the stem. Rebuild the scrolls as a few large, continuous S and C stems that start at the cartouche and wind out to the corners. Lobed acanthus leaves should grow off the stems: a central vein, secondary veins, three to five serrated lobes, and turned-over tips. Shading should be dark in the curl and light on the turned edge. At the moment the clusters at 548 (top corners, the mid-left and mid-right claws, the bottom centre pair) look like floating stickers, which reads as 'haphazard'.

Repetitive stamping: the bottom frieze at 548, below the beading, is a row of near-identical curl stamps. The short (90) plate is the same scroll unit four times, mirrored. The on-page 263 plate has a row of small identical curl stamps along the base above the pedestal. Replace all of these with one flowing running scroll that changes as it travels: a single stem whose curls alternate in size and direction.

Mt. Hood is drawn as a straight-sided pyramid. It needs Hood's real asymmetric profile: the steep north face, the long south-west shoulder, and the Illumination Rock bump. It needs a clearly white, engraved snow cap with glacier tongues and dark rock ribs. At present the snow cap and glaciers from the description cannot be read. The fir line is a uniform comb of identical spikes; vary the heights and add depth layers.

Pedestal and year tablet at 548 read as a flat CAD box, not a carved architectural piece. There are blank white bars: the tablet's left and right ends, the area to the right of the progress bar, and the plain white ribbon. These break the no-white rule. The rosettes are tiny clip-art. Give the plinth real mouldings: a knurled bar shaded in the round, an ogee with gradated hatching, and beads that carry a highlight and a shadow. Engrave the tablet face, and make the 86% progress read as a carved band with legible month ticks.

The ribbon banner is a plain white strip, and its Roman date is tiny and thin. Shade the ribbon's twists and folds with hatching, make the ends forked and turned under, and cut the capitals larger and heavier so that XI · XI · MMXXVI reads clearly on e-ink.

The hourglass crest finial is tiny and reads as a small icon on a stick. Make it a properly scaled, modelled finial with turned, shaded posts and visible sand, and grow it out of the leafwork the way the Codex's urn finial does.

On the page (263) the plate sits in a hard rectangular box. A frame line runs along its top and sides, and the strip of horizontal hatch above it shows a seam against the page's diagonal ground. It does not flow from the list above. Drop the boxed edge, let the top scrolls rise into the page ground, and blend the plate's ground into the page hatching.

The scene is not tied to today's content. The page is 'This day in history / Born today' (actors, an activist, a tennis player, a rugby player). Apart from the open book, nothing in the vignette speaks to births or history. Consider the book showing a candle or a birth-register motif, or carving small figural references to today's entries into the scroll (a tennis racquet, a rugby ball, theatre masks).
Easter egg: the swing-rhythm bar is plain rectangular square-wave glyphs and reads as a glitch, not as notes. Engrave real paired eighth notes with heads, stems and beams in a long-short pattern.

There is no figural element grown out of the scroll. The brief calls for figures carved into the leafwork, like the Codex's faces. Every element here is pasted on. Grow at least one figure (Hood's ridge, a heron's neck, the St. Johns arches) out of a scroll terminal.

Overall verdict: technically within budget, but it reads as clip-art flourishes on a striped ground and would not make Parker say wow. The horizontal-line ground is flat and uniform everywhere; vary it with stipple and denser cut-away near the relief so the scrolls pop.

The acanthus is not sculpted. The leaves are flat sawtooth blades with jagged zigzag edges and grid cross-hatch pasted inside the outline. Nothing is dark in the curl and light on the turned edge, and there are no midribs or secondary veins following the form. Rebuild the leaves as overlapping lobed acanthus with curved bulino hatch that follows each lobe's curvature, plus a highlight gap on the turned edges, as in codex-crop.jpg and hunt-crop.jpg.

The scrolls do not flow. The volutes are separate fragments ('C' hooks, claw-like leaf bits) scattered over the ground instead of one continuous stem that spirals into tight curls and branches. This is the 'haphazard' look Parker already rejected. Each half needs one or two big continuous S-scrolls growing out of the cartouche, with the leaves sheathing the stems.

The ground is wallpaper. The uniform horizontal line field behind everything reads as cheap and flat. Cut the background away as a darker, tighter ground with the hatch direction varying around the forms, or stipple it, so the relief pops locally. The same flat line field also fills the 548 pedestal zone.

548 frieze: the bottom band is a row of identical repeated stamps (curl, sprig, curl, sprig), which is exactly what the brief forbids. Replace it with one continuous running scroll, or drop it and let the pedestal end the plate.

548 top edge: a hard rectangular box and rule lines at the top read as a framed box, not a plate rising from the content. Use a moulding or scroll tips instead. The crest is a small spindly spike cluster. Make it a real carved crest, such as a fir-cone finial wrapped in leafwork.

Pedestal: plain thin-ruled boxes with two little rosettes and thin monoline lettering, nothing like the Codex's heavy knurled, shaded slab. Give it depth (a shaded top face, knurled bars, a shadowed undercut) and heavier engraved serif lettering. The banner lettering 'ST. JOHNS · MCMXXXI' is also thin and weak, and the ribbon has no twist or shaded folds.

Bridge vignette is crude. Mt. Hood is a flat pyramid triangle and the water is broken dash marks. The Cathedral Park arches are two black blobs and the firs are scribbly triangles. The towers are plain bars, without the Gothic stacked lancets the engraver describes. The heron is a stick figure. It needs engraved sky gradation, a snow-capped Hood with ridge shading, real ripple lines and a properly drawn green-steel Gothic tower silhouette.

The 240 plate has grape-like clusters in the top corners. They read as grapes, not Douglas-fir cones. Draw real cones with scale texture or remove them. The volutes are again disjointed blade fragments.

90 frieze: mirrored blade fragments around an oval sticker medallion, so it reads as a medallion pasted on a striped band. Make it a continuous carved scroll band with the bridge cartouche growing out of the stems.

No personal figure grows out of the leafwork in the way the Codex grows its faces. A scroll could curl into the heron's neck, or the bridge arches could become a scroll. Right now the heron only sits inside the vignette.

E-ink: the ground and leaf cross-hatch flatten into mid-grey with little tonal separation between the leaves and the background. Add contrast: a darker ground, leaf highlights that stay white, and fewer grid cross-hatches.
civics: 550x548: large blank white areas break the no-white rule. These include the top band above the frame (y 0-65, apart from where the leaves poke through), the white wedges at the top corners, the left and right margins beside the lower acanthus panel (about x 0-85 and 1055-1140, y 1010-1110), the gutter between the frame and the pedestal at the right, and the blank strips on the pedestal cornice. Extend the dark cut-away ground and the frame to all four edges of the canvas.

550x548: the pedestal is a hard rectangular box pasted across the bottom, with a second, narrower box of leaf fragments hung under it. The leaves are cut off by the cornice. The scrolls need to flow over and around the pedestal the way they do in the Codex, with the base scrolls under the pedestal as one big composition, not a strip of clipped sprigs.

Acanthus quality: the leaves read as spiky, jagged, saw-toothed shells or lobster claws, not sculpted acanthus. They have no clear central vein, no rolled lobes, and no confident spiral eyes (the 'eyes' are small black dots in thin C-hooks). The hatching is uniform parallel line fill, not shading that follows the form and goes dark into the curl. Rebuild the leaf vocabulary from the Hunt and Codex references: overlapping rolled lobes, a turned-over light edge, and dark cuts into the curl.

The herons are unreadable. On either side of the cartouche at 548 they appear only as a small hooked beak on a long tube, and at reading distance they look like more leaf fragments. In the Codex the bearded faces are the largest, most finished figures on the page. Make the herons big and recognisable, with modelled heads, crest plumes and neck feathers in bulino, growing out of the scroll.

The Capitol vignette is flat line art: a rectangle drum, outline columns, a stick-figure Pioneer, two blobby cloud-like trees, and a ruled-grid plaza. It needs engraved volume: shading on the drum and flutes, shadowed wings, a real Pioneer figure, foliage made with stipple, and a modelled flag. The ballot box, which is the Easter egg, is a small outlined box with an X. The crossed drumsticks with bead tips can't be read at any size. Enlarge and model them so the egg actually rewards a close look.

The cartouche frame is a plain rounded square with thick parallel rules, the same shape at 240 and 548. It is generic and box-like. Give it a carved, shaped cartouche with mouldings, beading and leaf tips breaking its edge.

WE THE PEOPLE banner: a flat thin strip with small type. The ends aren't folded or shaded, and it doesn't wrap around the scrolls. Give the ribbon curl-back ends with shading in the folds, and set bigger engraved lettering.

550x90 short frieze: four nearly identical leaf clusters repeat symmetrically, which is exactly the repetitive stamping the brief forbids. The beaded rule on top plus a plain rule below reads as wallpaper border. Build one continuous scroll that grows out of the medallion and runs to both ends, varying as it goes. Fix the engraver's return text too, which is cut off at 'The short frieze is'.

550x240 medium: the big volutes on the left and right mirror each other identically, and the clipped half-leaves at the four corners look cropped from a tile. There is a white gap between the top bead row and the ground. Let the volutes overlap and flow continuously to the ends.

The ground is the same horizontal line ruling everywhere, at every height. It is fine as a ground, but the plate reads as one flat tone. Add stipple and tonal variation behind the relief so the figures pop the way they do in the Codex.

TALL (548): the scrollwork is six separate, mirror-copied leaf clumps floating on a striped ground. Read as a whole, it looks like stickers, not one composition. Rebuild it as two continuous C/S scroll systems, one per side. Each should grow from the pedestal, wrap the cartouche, overlap itself and spiral into tight eyes, with leaves that turn over the stem, like codex-crop.jpg. No orphaned clumps (bottom-centre pair, the tiny corner spirals at top-left and top-right).

ACANTHUS QUALITY: the leaves are jagged saw-tooth blades with uniform parallel hatching. They have no central vein, no lobed serrations, no turned-over lip and no dark-into-the-curl shading. Model each leaf as in the reference: bulino that swells dark into the fold and fades to white at the turned edge, cross-hatch only in the deepest shadow, and a real spiral eye at every curl (not a black dot).

EAGLE CREST: it reads as a cartoon parrot or peacock with a fan of tubes. Redraw it as a heraldic bald eagle: a white-head feather texture, a hooked beak, spread wings of layered primaries that resolve into acanthus fingers and feed into the side scrolls, and talons gripping the cartouche top.

VIGNETTE: the Capitol is small and drafted flat, like a line diagram. Mt. Hood is a hatched pyramid with a zig-zag snowline, not a mountain with gullies. The Senate flag is missing on the tall and medium plates. The dome reflection is a grey smudge, and it turns to mud in -eink. Enlarge the Capitol to about 55% of the cartouche width. Give the dome ribs and drum columns cylindrical shading, light from upper left. Give Hood ridge-following gully hatching with a white snowfield. Add the flag. Draw the reflection as broken horizontal water lines carrying the dome silhouette.

RIBBON AND LETTERING: 'WE THE PEOPLE' is a thin strip in single-stroke sans lettering, lost against the scrolls. 'VOX · POPULI' is a small monoline caption in a big empty grey tablet with two token rosettes. Make the ribbon wide, with folded and shaded tails that curl behind the scrolls. Use engraved double-line Roman capitals with serifs for both legends, and fill the tablet so it reads as carved stone, sized like PRO AMORE ARTIS in the reference.

PEDESTAL AND EDGES: the pedestal is flat ruled bars plus a hatched band. Give it the reference's knurled torus bars with real knurl shading, a shaded cornice and a spreading base. The top edge is a straight bead line over a rule, a hard box lid. Let scroll tips and the crest break above the top line so the plate rises from the content.

MEDIUM (240): it is two identical mirrored clusters plus four corner spiral stamps. The large volutes do not run out to the ends. Leaves are cut off at the corners, and the knurled foot is only a thin hatched line. Build one continuous volute from the cartouche to each end, with a cartouche frame that has carved relief (not concentric rules) and a real knurled foot.

SHORT (90): four near-identical leaf clumps in a row, which is exactly the repetitive stamping Parker rejected. Replace them with one running scroll per side, a single continuous rinceau that leaves the oval and diminishes toward the ends. The flag here is a flat sticker, so engrave it.

SHADING DENSITY (the main gap against the Codex): the hatching is coarse, about 3-4 px pitch with heavy strokes. The Codex uses very fine bulino, roughly 1-1.5 px pitch at 2x, with tonal gradation that runs from near-black in the curl throats through mid-grey to a thin white highlight on the turned edge. Halve the line pitch and stroke width, add a second and third cross-hatch pass in the deep zones, and taper the line weight along each hatch so the tone rolls instead of stepping.

VOLUTES READ AS FLAT CUT-PAPER CLAWS, NOT ACANTHUS. Every leaf is a large white silhouette with a jagged sawtooth edge and a little hatch patch. There are no central veins, no secondary veins, no serrated lobes that fold over one another, and no rounded leaf tips curling back. The scrolls are also broken into separate claw fragments; they need one continuous spiral stem that winds into a tight spiral eye with a beaded centre, as in the Codex, not a black dot on a C-hook. Rebuild the volutes as continuous S- and C-scrolls with overlapping leaves cloaking the stem.

TOO MUCH WHITE: the leaf bodies, the cartouche frame rings (550x240), the ribbon 'VOTE MAY 18', the scene road/fields, the sky above Hood, the capitol facade and the drop box are all large blank or near-blank areas well over 12x12 px. Engrave the sky with fine graded horizontal lines (darker at the top), lay water lines on the Willamette, give the fields furrow hatching, shade the ribbon folds and the undersides of its twists, and put a hatched shadow side on the frame mouldings.

CUT-AWAY GROUND IS WALLPAPER: one uniform horizontal line field sits behind everything, at every height. The Codex ground is a dark stippled or cross-hatched cut-away that deepens next to the relief so the scrolls pop. Darken the ground near the leaf edges and vary it, and add cast shadows from the volutes onto it.

MEDIUM 550x240 SCENE: the wide white road with converging lines dominates and looks like clip art. The Willamette, the valley fields and the heron are illegible (the heron is a tiny smudge top right). Mt. Hood is a flat triangle with zig-zag snow; it needs ridges, glaciers and a light/dark flank modelled in bulino. The drop box is a flat outlined box, and the ballot X drumsticks are unreadable at this scale. Enlarge the heron so it reads as a heron (neck S-curve, trailing legs, feather hatching) and make the drumsticks clearly two sticks with ball tips.

SHORT 550x90: four nearly identical claw-scroll units stamped symmetrically around a plain envelope medallion is the repetitive stamping we banned. The envelope is a flat outline on a white oval with a generic circled X, and the drumstick egg does not read. Make one continuous running scroll that flows out of the medallion to both ends, and model the envelope with paper shading, a wax seal with relief, and crossed drumsticks with ball tips.

TALL 550x548: the capitol is a flat stack of boxes and the Golden Pioneer is a stick figure. It needs a fluted drum with a shaded cylinder, a lantern, and a gilt pioneer figure. The bottom frieze is again separate stamped claws on lines. The pedestal is good in concept but flat: it needs knurled bars and beaded mouldings with real cylinder shading like the Codex's knurled rails, and the '188 DAYS' tablet should be a recessed, shaded panel. The top scroll masses are disconnected leaf fragments floating on the ground.

LETTERING: 'VOTE MAY 18' and '188 DAYS' are thin monoline sans in white boxes and read as UI labels. Draw engraved display letters (shaded serif or block caps with a cut shadow), as in the Codex's 'HAND ENGRAVING' banner, and curve them with the ribbon.

E-INK: the 240 view holds up tonally but goes flat grey everywhere. There is no true black accent, so nothing pops. Reserve a solid black for the deepest curl throats and the cartouche's inner shadow.

The acanthus is not Codex-grade. The leaves read as stiff claw or pine-cone feathers with sawtooth edges. They do not roll into big C and S scrolls with tight spiral eyes. Leaves need a central vein, secondary veins, lobes that turn over and show their underside, and bulino shading that runs dark into the curl and light on the turned edge. Right now each leaf has one flat hatch angle plus a crosshatch patch.

The scrolls do not flow or overlap. At 548 the four corner masses are separate mirrored clumps, and the floating sprigs between them (top centre, the bottom row above the pedestal, the bottom band) read as pasted-on stickers. Make one continuous scroll system that grows from a base stem, wraps the cartouche, and overlaps itself the way the reference does.

There is repetitive stamping. The running-dog top moulding at 548 and 240 is a row of identical little spiral stamps. The 90 px frieze is the same leaf cluster repeated four times around the medallion. The bottom band at 548 is four or five evenly spaced identical sprigs. All of these break the 'no repeated stamps' rule.

The wave does not turn into the scrollwork. The 'acanthus-finger spray claws' on the lip read as a row of small white teeth or blobs stuck on the crest, and the black barrel is a flat solid hole. Draw the lip as a real curling acanthus volute that sweeps from the frame into the wave, model the barrel with graded hatching rather than a black void, and build the face from tone-graded curved bulino.

The figures are weak. The heron is a thin flat outline with no feather bulino, and it barely reads as the Easter egg. The surfer is a tiny silhouette. The clouds are flat semicircle stamps. The spruce ridge on Tillamook Head is a zigzag line, and the lighthouse is a speck. Each needs real engraved modelling.

There are blank white areas. The ribbon interior is plain white, flat and untwisted, with no shading on the turned ends. The pedestal tablet sides are largely plain hatch boxes. Lighting the scroll interiors and the small white blocks in the moulding risks failing the 12×12 rule. The ribbon must twist, with shaded folds and dark undersides.

There are hard boxes. At 240 the cartouche is a thick rounded-square frame and the plate ends in a hard bottom rule. At 548 the pedestal is a stack of ruled boxes, and the bottom band is cut off at the plate edge with sprigs clipped. The plate should hang from the content with scroll tips, not a boxed frame.

In the e-ink render (548-eink), the horizontal-line ground plus the horizontal-line pedestal gives large flat mid-grey fields with no relief. The scroll masses wash out to similar values, so nothing pops. A darker cut-away ground behind the scrolls (crosshatch or stipple) is needed so the relief separates.
The lettering ('SEASIDE COVE' and the tablet reading) is thin single-stroke sans. It needs engraved, weighted serif or banner lettering with shaded drop, as in the reference.
